title: lb-sticky-session-induced-canary-degradation-postmortem
summary: A canary rollout on 2024-10-18 experienced a sustained p95 latency degradation and partial output corruption for ~46 minutes. Root cause: unexpected session-affinity (LB sticky sessions) combined with staggered weight apply semantics on the canary fleet which caused a subset of client connections to continuously hit partially-rolled nodes with stale KV-cache state. The mismatch led to frequent rehydration, decode retries, and tokenization fallbacks on the serving runtime.
detection: Alert: serving.p95.latency > SLO (5s) for model 'redwood-llama-13b-quant' in us-west-2-canary. Pager triggered at 2024-10-18T09:12:03Z by the observability pipeline (route-level p95 > 5s). On-call saw anomalous increase in 'model.decode.retries' metric and a spike in 'tokenization.fallback' events. Slack #sre-incident channel auto-created at 09:13.
timeline:
09:05 - 09:10 UTC: Canary rollout initiated (batch weight-swap across 20 canary nodes).
09:11 UTC: First latency p95 alerts from us-west-2-canary.
09:12 UTC: On-call acknowledges, starts triage.
09:15 UTC: Traces show long tail on first-request after connection (KV cache miss churn).
09:18 UTC: Noticed connection-level traces all map back to a small subset of LBs with session-affinity enabled.
09:20 UTC: Temporary mitigation: disabled session-affinity for canary LBs.
09:23 UTC: Latency partially improved but tokenization fallback events persisted.
09:28 UTC: Reverted weight-swap on canary (roll back to previous model binary) while continuing to flush KV caches.
09:40 UTC: Metrics returned to baseline; incidents closed at 09:58 after 3 verification cycles.
Total duration (from alert to steady-state): ~46 minutes.
impact:
- Customer-facing SLOs: p95 latency breach for ~46 minutes in us-west-2 canary route.
- Internal: increased error budget consumption on canary traffic, several ephemeral degraded responses observed in synthetic tests.
- No broad production user impact; canary traffic is limited to 2% of routed requests but some internal customers using canary flag experienced degraded quality.
root_cause:
Primary issue: Load balancer session-affinity (IP-hash cookie) configured by an infra change earlier that day was applied to the canary LB pool. Session-affinity caused some long-lived client connections to continuously target a small subset of canary instances. Those instances were simultaneously undergoing a staggered weight-apply sequence where the runtime applies new weight shards in-place over a 30s window. When a connection repeatedly hit a node mid-apply, we observed:
- Partial weight state (layer groups updated, others not),
- KV cache state tied to prior weight layout causing mismatched KV keys and frequent cache rehydration,
- Runtime falling back to slower decode paths and triggering tokenization fallback logic.
Contributing factors: lack of a guard that disables session-affinity for canary pools, and the staggered in-place weight-apply semantics without connection drain awareness.
mitigation_and_resolution:
1) Immediate: disabled session-affinity on canary load balancers (09:20 UTC) which distributed new connections across the canary pool and allowed healthy nodes to absorb traffic.
2) Rolled back the weight-swap on canary fleet to previous stable binary (09:28 UTC) to avoid further mid-apply states.
3) Flushed KV caches on affected nodes and restarted the serving processes on the 6 nodes with highest error counts.
4) Post-incident: added LB config check to pre-rollout checklist and a pre-flight test to assert session-affinity is disabled for any canary pool.
All steps executed by on-call SRE (Aditya R) and infra (Eleni V) with coordination from serving-runtime lead (Jordan P).
runbook_changes:
- Add explicit pre-rollout validation step: 'LB session-affinity must be OFF for canary pools' (checklist and automated assertion).
- Update weight-apply procedure: if in-place apply is used, enable connection draining on targeted instances OR switch to 'drain-then-apply' flow.
- Add an observability rule: if model.weight.apply_in_progress AND serving.p95.latency spikes for same nodes, open high-priority checklist.
- Add synthetic canary test to validate tokenization consistency post-weight-apply (run a standard prompt set immediately after apply completes).
action_items:
- SRE: implement LB config pre-flight automation (owner: Aditya Rao, due: 2024-11-01).
- Infra: add an option to disable session-affinity by default for canary pools and document rationale (owner: Eleni Vassiliou, due: 2024-10-25).
- Serving runtime: prototype a 'drain-then-apply' weight rollout mode and test on staging (owner: Jordan Park, due: 2024-11-15).
- Observability: add cross-metric alert for weight-apply + p95 spike (owner: Priya Menon, due: 2024-10-30).
- QA: add tokenization/kv-consistency checks into prelaunch smoke (owner: QA team, contact: Samir), due 2024-11-05.
postmortem_notes:
- This incident is an intersection of infra-level LB behavior + application-level rollout semantics. Previously we assumed canary pools would inherit 'no affinity' but a last-minute infra tweak flipped the default.
- The staggered weight-apply without drain is an optimization for capacity but has a correctness surface area when combined with sticky clients.
- The tokenization fallback metric was the earliest reliable indicator; consider promoting that to a canary-specific early-warning signal.
- We were able to recover quickly because canary traffic fraction is small and rollback path is fast; if this happened in production pool the impact would be higher.
- Keep this incident as a case study for cross-team rollout coordination: infra + serving-runtime + SRE must sign off.
communication:

- Customer Success notified of possible minor internal regressions at 10:05 UTC.
- Postmortem draft will be shared with Eng infra and Serving leads and then with broader Eng and CS teams the week after (2024-10-21 review).
open_questions:
- Why did the infra change flip session-affinity default for this LB pool only? (infra config drift or human mistake?)
- Can we detect 'mid-apply' connection affinity programmatically and mitigate without full rollback?
- Are there any long-tail clients that maintain persistent connections from before the disable change that still route to affected nodes? We need a connection dump analysis (next action).
